original_title: Synthesis of the N -Alkoxyguanidinyl Spiroketal Core of Rugonidines A–F
title: First synthesis of the rugonidine spiroketal core
blurb: A one-pot deprotection/cyclization cascade builds the [4.5]-fused N-alkoxyguanidinyl spiroketal that defines rugonidines A-F, confirmed by X-ray. Nine steps for 21% yield, so nobody's scaling this up, but it's the first time anyone's actually built and seen that ring system in the solid state.

original_title: Engineering and preclinical development of hydrogels for dermatologic drug delivery.
title: Getting drugs through skin, hydrogel edition
blurb: A look at the engineering and preclinical progress on hydrogels built specifically for dermatologic drug delivery.

original_title: New Antibody-Drug Conjugate SCR-A008 Shows Powerful Tumor Suppression in Gastric Cancer Models - Bioengineer.org
title: SCR-A008 knocks back gastric tumors, in the company's own models
blurb: An antibody-drug conjugate, SCR-A008, is reported to strongly suppress tumor growth in gastric cancer models. Reads like a straight announcement with no independent numbers attached, so treat it as a first data point, not a result.

original_title: Discovery of G2019S Mutant Selective LRRK2 Inhibitors Based on an Indazole Octahydrocyclopenta[ c ]pyrrole-Based Hybrid Chemotype
title: A LRRK2 inhibitor that prefers the Parkinson's mutant
blurb: Swapping a piperidine for an octahydrocyclopenta[c]pyrrole widens the selectivity window between wild-type and G2019S-mutant LRRK2 while keeping potency, where the piperidine version worked fine but barely told the two apart.

original_title: Metal Fluorides: All-In-One Supports for Ruthenium-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
title: Ammonia catalysis gets a menu of fluoride supports
blurb: One family of metal fluoride supports (Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, Ba) for ruthenium ammonia synthesis, and swapping the cation swaps the catalytic pathway rather than just tweaking it. Ru/NaF wins on turnover frequency while Ru/BaF2 is built for a different part of the job, same Ru, same idea, different host doing the steering.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: The Chemistry of Chirality : Molecular Handedness, Asymmetric Synthesis, Chemical Symmetry Breaking, and the Emergence of Biological Homochirality
title: A grand tour of why molecules pick a hand
blurb: A sweep through chirality as a topic: asymmetric synthesis, symmetry breaking, and how biology ended up stuck with one handedness. This is scaffolding, not a result, the kind of survey other papers assume you've already read.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Modular synthesis of 3,3-diaryloxetanes
title: A way around the Friedel-Crafts wall for diaryloxetanes
blurb: 3,3-diaryloxetanes are a useful diaryl ketone bioisostere in drug design, but making them has mostly meant Lewis acid Friedel-Crafts chemistry that only tolerates electron-rich arenes and wrecks sensitive functional groups along the way. This is a modular route pitched as a fix for exactly that bottleneck.

original_title: Building better therapeutic antibodies: the science, progress and problems to solve - Drug Target Review
title: What's actually hard about making a better antibody drug
blurb: An industry rundown of where therapeutic antibody development still gets stuck, framed as science, progress, and the unsolved problems in between. Not much more on offer than the framing itself.

original_title: Development and study of a novel anti-HER2 therapeutic conjugate based on DARPin G3
title: Swapping the antibody in a HER2 conjugate for a DARPin
blurb: DARPins bind tightly, hold up to heat, and express cleanly in bacteria, which makes them a plausible stand-in for full antibodies in protein-drug conjugates. This one targets HER2 with the G3 DARPin carrying the cytotoxic payload, and the actual work here is the unglamorous part everyone skips: getting the analytical characterization and standardization right.

original_title: Ligand-Derived Effects in N , C -Cyclometalated Palladium(II) Acetate Dimers
title: What the ligand actually does inside a cyclometalated Pd(II) dimer
blurb: A set of N,C-cyclometalated Pd(II) acetate dimers, one series varying the aryl ring and another the azole, all confirmed by X-ray as acetate-bridged dimers with a real structural trans influence. Pd1 locks into a single transoid isomer while Pd2 through Pd5 sit as transoid/cisoid mixtures, so sterics and trans influence are doing visibly different work depending on which end of the ligand gets changed.

original_title: A photoinduced, FeX3-catalyzed, stereo- and regio-selective halofunctionalization of olefins with MXn via a radical-polar crossover reaction
title: Iron and light put the halogen exactly where you want it on an olefin
blurb: An FeX3 photocatalyst runs a radical-polar crossover to halofunctionalize olefins with controlled stereochemistry and regiochemistry using MXn reagents. Iron and visible light doing a job that's usually handed to heavier, pricier catalysts.

original_title: Copper-Mediated Nitrogen-Atom Migration into Saturated Carbocycles
title: Swapping a ring carbon for nitrogen, one step, no rebuild
blurb: Turning a saturated carbocycle into a medicinally relevant heterocycle usually means starting over, since C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds don't activate on command. This is a one-step formal nitrogen insertion that runs through nitrogen-centered radicals to trigger the ring rearrangement directly, a shortcut for remodeling carbocyclic drug leads into the heterocycles people actually want.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A Peripheral Sulfonium Moiety Engineering Strategy to Enhance AIEgen-Based Antitumor Photodynamic Therapy
title: A sulfonium tweak makes this photosensitizer less picky about oxygen
blurb: Adding a peripheral sulfonium group to an AIE photosensitizer (lead compound S12) boosts spin-orbit coupling and shrinks the singlet-triplet gap, which means more reactive oxygen species. The real payoff is that S12 makes both Type I and Type II ROS at once, so its photodynamic activity only weakly depends on oxygen, which matters for the hypoxic tumors where most PDT runs out of steam.

original_title: Chiral Solid-State Nanopores Amplify Secondary Interactions for Ionic-Current Discrimination of Neurotransmitter Enantiomers
title: Nanopores that can tell left-handed neurotransmitters from right
blurb: A beta-cyclodextrin/trimesoyl chloride membrane layered onto TiO2 nanopores, with L-tryptophan parked in the host-guest pocket to amplify the weak, short-lived interactions that normally make enantiomers indistinguishable by ionic current. Single-molecule sensing taking on stereochemistry, which is usually the part these methods fumble.

original_title: Diffusion-Limited Solid-State Synthesis Selectivity in the Presence of Oxidation/Reduction Processes
title: Redox makes solid-state synthesis selectivity harder to predict
blurb: The existing framework ties phase selectivity in solid-state synthesis to ion mobility inside liquid-like amorphous interphases, first shown in the Ba-Ti-O system. This extends it to precursors that change valence state mid-reaction, which complicates the ion transport deciding which phase wins out.

original_title: Honeycomb Structured ZnO Nanosheets: A Dual Platform for Ultrasensitive Nitrite Sensing and Organic Catalysis
title: ZnO honeycombs that moonlight as a nitrite sensor and a catalyst
blurb: Honeycomb-structured ZnO nanosheets built to do two jobs at once off the same material: ultrasensitive nitrite detection and organic catalysis.

original_title: Tuning the Architecture of High-Density Bottlebrush Block Copolymers to Control Their Photonic Properties
title: Bottlebrush copolymers get a fifth branch, and the photonics follow
blurb: Backbone rigidity in bottlebrush block copolymers has been capped at two branches per repeat unit because synthesis couldn't manage more. This group used graft-through ROMP to build PS-b-PLA5, five PLA branches per unit, pushing past that ceiling and with it the rigidity that drives these polymers' fast photonic self-assembly.

original_title: Programming Hydrophobic Nanocavity of DNA Frameworks for Ultrastable Fluorescent Imaging
title: DNA cages built to hold a dye still enough to actually image with it
blurb: Fluorescent proteins are convenient but hard to tune. These DNA framework dots sidestep that by parking Cy3 inside a hydrophobic nanocavity built from tetrahedral DNA frameworks with alkyl chains pointed inward, giving a programmable, ultrastable dye carrier for imaging instead.

original_title: Synthesis of chitosan/polypyrrole membranes for application in PEM fuel cells
title: Chitosan and polypyrrole team up for a fuel-cell membrane
blurb: A plasma-doped chitosan/polypyrrole membrane for PEM fuel cells, sulfonated afterward to graft on -SO3H groups for proton transport (confirmed by FTIR). Chitosan supplies the structural, proton-conducting matrix, polypyrrole does the rest.

original_title: Cysteine-based molecular switches: a focus on KEAP1 and BACH1 in regulating the antioxidant response
title: KEAP1 and BACH1, the cysteine switches deciding how hard your cells fight oxidants
blurb: A review of how reactive cysteines on KEAP1 and the repressor BACH1 act as the cell's own redox sensors, flipping on the antioxidant response once their thiols get hit by oxidants or electrophiles. Mechanism synthesis, not new data.

original_title: Catching enhanced flexibility in antibody-antigen recognition: critical evaluation of physics-based and AI-driven methods
title: Antibody-antigen docking, now admitting the proteins actually flex
blurb: A critical look at whether physics-based models or AI methods actually capture the flexibility antibodies and antigens show when binding, rather than treating both as rigid. Reads as a head-to-head evaluation of the two camps rather than a win for either.

original_title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Quinoxaline Derivatives as Anticancer Agents Targeting EGFR Pathways
title: Another quinoxaline aimed at EGFR, strong so far on the computer
blurb: Novel quinoxaline derivatives synthesized as EGFR-targeted anticancer agents, with docking showing favorable binding to key EGFR residues. Clean computational story for now, so it comes down to how the compounds actually perform in the biological assays.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

original_title: 15 U.S. sites make medicines used in PET scans. GE HealthCare has agreed to buy SOFIE Biosciences. - Stock Titan
title: GE HealthCare buys up a PET-drug maker
blurb: GE HealthCare has agreed to acquire SOFIE Biosciences, one of just 15 US sites that make the radioactive medicines used in PET scans. Consolidation in a pretty narrow, bottlenecked supply chain.

original_title: Beyond the binding site: PROTAC-mediated protein degradation assists the therapeutic paradigm of hematological malignancies.
title: PROTACs go after blood cancer targets from somewhere other than the binding site
blurb: A review on using PROTAC-style degraders against hematological malignancies, built around the idea that degradation just needs a handle on the protein, not a fit into its canonical binding pocket. Survey piece, not new trial results.

original_title: 100 ns molecular dynamics of cocaine bound to the human dopamine transporter (DAT)
title: 100 ns molecular dynamics of cocaine bound to the human dopamine transporter (DAT)
blurb: I recently ran a 100 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulation of cocaine bound to the human dopamine transporter (DAT), starting from the experimentally determined cocaine-bound structure PDB 9EO4. The main thing I wanted to look at was whether the bound cocaine pose remained stable after equilibration and how the protein–ligand interaction network evolved over time. Across the 100 ns trajectory, cocaine remained very stable relative to DAT, with a mean protein-aligned ligand RMSD of about 1.17 Å. DAT itself also remained stable, with a mean Cα RMSD of about 1.55 Å. Some of the more persisten

original_title: Prepared a stable carbocation that formed these shiny golden balls during vacuum evaporation
title: Prepared a stable carbocation that formed these shiny golden balls during vacuum evaporation

original_title: Development of a Hyaluronic Acid−Retinol Conjugate for Enhanced Photostability and Transdermal Delivery
title: Retinol gets a sugar coat to stop falling apart in the sun
blurb: Retinol works but barely survives light, barely dissolves in water, and gets cytotoxic past a certain dose. Conjugating it to hyaluronic acid, confirmed by NMR, HPLC, and FTIR, is pitched as fixing the photostability problem and improving delivery through skin. Standard chemistry-paper fix for a molecule that's been fighting its own formulation for decades.

original_title: Methods for inferring interaction potentials from cross-linking mass spectrometry data
title: Turning crosslinking MS data into an actual force field
blurb: XL-MS gives pairwise distance constraints between proteins at scale, but converting that into coarse-grained interaction potentials has mostly meant brute-force fitting of radial distribution functions. This argues for fitting coordination numbers instead, since they're functionals of the RDF that direct fitting can't properly capture. A methods paper, but it's addressing a real bottleneck for anyone building particle models off crosslinking data.

original_title: Oxidation of H -Phosphonate Diesters by Oxyma-Based Coupling Reagents
title: Your coupling reagent might be oxidizing your H-phosphonates on the side
blurb: COMU, TOMBU, PyOxim, and DIC/oxymaPure all turn out to oxidize H-phosphonate diesters, an oxidative pathway nobody had pinned on these now-standard Oxyma-based peptide coupling reagents. Benzotriazole-based reagents don't do it, and HOMO-LUMO gap analysis backs up why. Worth a second look if you've been coupling phosphonate-bearing substrates with Oxyma chemistry and wondering about side products.

original_title: Capillary Gel Electrophoresis Separation of dsDNA Molecules Using Tetrahydroxyborate Stabilized Hydroxyethyl Cellulose – Polyvinylpyrrolidone Physical Copolymer
title: A borate-crosslinked gel for sorting dsDNA by capillary electrophoresis
blurb: Built for the nucleic-acid-therapeutics boom: a dual-network hydrogel of hydroxyethyl cellulose and polyvinylpyrrolidone, with boric acid forming spiroborane bridges that crosslink and stabilize the HEC network while also suppressing electroosmotic flow. Unglamorous polymer chemistry, but it's exactly the kind of separation matrix that decides whether your dsDNA run actually resolves.

original_title: Integrated [<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-FAPI-7ND PET/CT and stromal profiling of immunocompetent syngeneic tumor models for FAP-targeted radionuclide therapy
title: Imaging FAP in mice that still have an immune system
blurb: Ga-68-FAPI-7ND PET/CT paired with stromal profiling, done in immunocompetent syngeneic tumor models rather than the usual immunodeficient mice, to back FAP as a target for radionuclide therapy. That detail matters: most FAP-targeting data comes from mice that can't tell you anything about how an intact immune system reacts to hitting the stroma.

original_title: Glycosylated Diarylmethyloxy-Triazines: Facile Synthesis and Aqueous Self-Assembly for Supramolecular Hydrogel Formation
title: Sugar-decorated triazines that self-assemble into hydrogels
blurb: A facile synthesis of glycosylated diarylmethyloxy-triazines that self-assemble in water into supramolecular hydrogels, with saccharides displayed on the surface the way real biological structures do. The selling point is the triazine scaffold's easy protecting-group chemistry, which is doing a lot of the work behind that nice self-assembly photo.

original_title: Chemical methods for O-GlcNAc detection and preparation of O-GlcNAc modified proteins
title: The chemistry toolkit that found and now reads O-GlcNAc
blurb: A review tracing chemistry's role in O-GlcNAc from the start: a radioactive sugar donor that enabled its discovery, then bioorthogonal metabolic labeling and chemoenzymatic tagging for visualizing and quantifying it in living systems, then solid-phase peptide synthesis for building defined O-GlcNAc-modified proteins. A map of which tricks unlocked which part of the biology, if you're coming to the field cold.

original_title: Direct Enantioselective α-Alkoxylation of β-Keto Esters Enabled by Umpolung Strategy
title: Flipping the polarity to put a chiral ether next to a ketone
blurb: Chiral ethers next to a carbonyl are useful and annoyingly hard to make asymmetrically from simple starting materials. Here an umpolung move activates alkyl hydroperoxides with trichloroacetonitrile so a chiral bifunctional organocatalyst can transfer the alkoxy group enantioselectively onto beta-keto esters. A workaround for a bond that's normally a coin flip on stereochemistry.

original_title: Cooperative Agostic‐Type C─H···Cu, Quadrupolar Cu···CO 2 , and C─H···O/π Interactions in an Ultra‐Microporous MOF Enable One‐Step Methane Purification From Quaternary C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 /CH 4
title: A MOF that purifies methane by grabbing everything that isn't methane
blurb: LIFM-XYY-15 is a phosphine-decorated, ultra-microporous copper MOF leaning on agostic C-H...Cu interactions, quadrupolar Cu...CO2 contacts, and C-H...O/π contacts to preferentially grab propane, ethane, and CO2 over methane, with reported uptake ratios up to 2.46, 2.30, and 3.92 against CH4. The part worth noticing is it does this in one step on an actual quaternary mixture, not a binary toy system.

original_title: γ‐Radionuclide Technetium‐99M Activated Long‐Lasting Chemodynamic Therapy and Immunogenic Brachytherapy for Enhanced Antitumor Immunity
title: Tc-99m's gamma rays moonlighting as a Fenton catalyst
blurb: A Hf-TCPP@Fe-99mTc MOF nanocomposite pairs chemodynamic therapy's Fenton chemistry with technetium-99m brachytherapy, using hafnium's high-Z boost to amplify the secondary electrons from the gamma emission. The authors say that drives both tumor damage and a stronger antitumor immune response, going after the two standard complaints about this combo: weak Fenton efficiency and brachytherapy's poor immunogenicity.

original_title: A VAPG Incorporating Targeted Self-Assembling Peptides for Efficient VSMC Restoring and Imaging in Abdominal Aortic Models
title: A self-assembling peptide that sticks around in aneurysm walls long enough to work
blurb: VSMC-recruiting peptides already existed, the problem was they clear out of the aneurysm site before doing anything useful. This one self-assembles on an enzyme trigger right in the lesion, buying local retention plus imaging in an abdominal aortic aneurysm model. Solves an actual delivery problem rather than just offering another targeting ligand.

original_title: Molecular and immune-mediated resistance to antibody-drug conjugates in breast cancer
title: ADCs stop working in breast cancer for reasons beyond the drug itself
blurb: A review of why antibody-drug conjugates in breast cancer eventually fail, across HER2-positive, HER2-low, and triple-negative disease, covering both molecular resistance and the immune mechanisms these drugs increasingly lean on. A map of failure modes, not a fix for any of them.

original_title: NovAccel Expands U.S. Presence to Advance Global Actinium-225 Supply - markets.businessinsider.com
title: NovAccel plants a flag in the US actinium-225 race
blurb: A supply-side move: NovAccel expanding its US presence to push global actinium-225 production. Standard corporate announcement, worth filing away rather than celebrating until actual output numbers show up.

original_title: An IscS Persulfide Donates the Sulfur for Ribosomal Protein uL16 Thioamidation
title: Found the sulfur source behind a weird ribosomal thioamide
blurb: Thousands of Pseudomonadota quietly swap an amide for a thioamide in ribosomal protein uL16, and this pins down where the sulfur comes from: IscS, the same cysteine desulfurase that feeds iron-sulfur cluster assembly. Ties a widespread but obscure modification to a pathway everyone already knew about.

original_title: High-throughput spatial proteomics from cellular to subcellular scales via a hanging droplet workflow
title: A 96-well way to get spatial proteomics out of old FFPE blocks
blurb: FFPE tissue is what pathology archives are full of, and mass spec hates it: extraction losses, evaporation during decrosslinking, fiddly prep. This hanging-droplet protocol runs laser-capture microdissected samples through a 96-well format instead, chasing throughput and depth down to subcellular scale. A workflow paper, but aimed at a genuinely annoying bottleneck.

original_title: Synthetic strategies toward 3-arylcoumarins: From classical condensation to sustainable C–H arylation
title: Everything anyone's tried to bolt an aryl onto coumarin's C3
blurb: A review walking from classic condensation through transition-metal coupling, radical and photoredox routes, mechanochemistry, and whatever counts as sustainable this year, all aimed at the same stubborn problem of making the C3-aryl bond cleanly. Organized by strategy rather than timeline, which is the only way these reviews are worth reading.

original_title: Electron Donor–Acceptor Complex Catalysis in Synthetic Chemistry
title: Making electron donor-acceptor complexes do catalysis, not just one-shot photochemistry
blurb: EDA complexes have long been a reliable way to kick off radical reactions with light, stoichiometrically. Turning that into an actual catalytic cycle means getting charge-transfer excitation to cooperate with catalyst regeneration, and that's the harder, more recent problem this review organizes design principles around.

original_title: Phosphorus(V) Umpolung Converts Electrophilic Phosphates into Nucleophilic H-Phosphonates
title: Flipping phosphate's polarity so it attacks instead of getting attacked
blurb: Phosphate groups are electrophilic and P-OH bonds are stubborn, which normally blocks late-stage conversion into other phosphate analogues, the kind used in phosphorothioate antisense drugs. This umpolung route thiolates the P-OH first, then uses that to flip phosphorus into a nucleophile, turning electrophilic phosphates into nucleophilic H-phosphonates. A real polarity trick, not just a new coupling partner.

original_title: Enantioselective Pericyclization of Naphthol-Substituted Alkynyl Ketimines
title: One pot, two ring systems, and a new route to axial chirality via 6π-azaelectrocyclization
blurb: An organocatalyzed tandem electrocyclization/spirocycloaddition on naphthol-substituted alkynyl ketimines, run through an NBS-triggered vinylidene quinone methide, spits out axially chiral 3-haloquinolines and a spirocyclic xanthenopyrrole scaffold nobody's made before. First intramolecular route to these biaryl quinolines this way, with high enantioselectivity and broad functional group tolerance by their account.

original_title: Unanticipated intermediates during isopenicillin N synthase catalysis identified by time-resolved X-ray free-electron laser studies
title: Caught isopenicillin N synthase's missing intermediates on an X-ray laser
blurb: The enzyme that builds penicillin's strained bicyclic ring has had two structural gaps for ages: the precursors right before the β-lactam and thiazolidine rings close. Time-resolved serial femtosecond crystallography plus X-ray emission spectroscopy on anaerobic IPNS:Fe(II):ACV crystals reacting with O2 finally catches those states directly, nailing down a mechanism people have been guessing at for decades.

original_title: Rapid selection of high-affinity DARPins using click display.
title: Click chemistry speeds up DARPin selection
blurb: Swapping click chemistry into the display step to link genotype to phenotype, aimed at pulling high-affinity DARPins out of a library faster than standard phage or ribosome display manage.

original_title: FtmOx1-catalyzed diverse C(sp3)-H oxyfunctionalization enables versatile late-stage diversification of phenethylamines and tetrahydroisoquinolines
title: An endoperoxidase that moonlights as an oxidation toolkit
blurb: FtmOx1 normally installs the endoperoxide in fumitremorgin B, but pointed at phenethylamines and tetrahydroisoquinolines it'll do β-hydroxylation, β-ketone formation, dealkylation, or α,β-desaturation depending on the substrate. Worked across 48 substrates, which is the kind of scope that actually makes a late-stage-diversification enzyme useful rather than a one-trick curiosity.

original_title: Chromoselective Control for Aminoalkylation of CF3‑Alkenes through Low-Energy Photoredox Catalysis
title: Picking the wavelength picks the product
blurb: Same photocatalyst, same N-arylglycine feedstock, but dialing the irradiation wavelength steers decarboxylative/defluorinative aminoalkylation of CF3-alkenes toward different sites on the molecule. HTE screening found the catalyst/wavelength pairs that make the switch clean, which is the whole point since nobody wants to run two separate reactions to get two products.

original_title: Cascade Remodeling through Late-Stage Electrophilic Fluorination in a Bis-Spiroketal Framework
title: Using fluorine to steer a cascade instead of just substituting it in
blurb: Electrophilic fluorination usually just swaps in a C-F bond, but here it traps transient nucleophiles mid-cascade and blocks the pathway that normally sends the molecule to degradation. Shown on a salinomycin derivative, where sequential fluorinations gate a multistep rearrangement that otherwise just falls apart. A deactivating group used as a control knob rather than an endpoint.

original_title: Wavelength-Selective Magneto-Optical Diodes Based on Rare-Earth Chiral Molecular Crystals
title: A crystal that reads light differently depending on which way it's going
blurb: Erbium-based chiral molecular crystals absorb light differently depending on which direction it's traveling, and the effect is tunable by wavelength and magnetic field, with swings up to about 200%. A genuine magneto-optical diode out of a molecular crystal rather than a bulk inorganic one.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Oxygen Evolution Electrocatalysts with Trinuclear, Mixed‐Valence Iron Motifs on Electronically Aligned Carbon Dots
title: Clustering iron three at a time to speed up oxygen evolution
blurb: Trinuclear Fe3+/Fe2+ motifs anchored on aspartic-acid-derived carbon dots bring redox flexibility to the handoff that usually bottlenecks oxygen evolution, the sluggish electron transfer at the interface. The scaffold's work function is tuned to pull electrons straight out of the bound hydroxide, going after the adsorbate scaling problem that limits most single-site OER catalysts.

original_title: Magnetically recyclable CoFe₂O₄@HKUST-1 nanocatalyst for sustainable carbon–nitrogen coupling, and structure-affinity relationship study of the synthesized products via molecular docking
title: A magnet you can fish back out of the alpha-ketoamide reaction
blurb: A cobalt ferrite core wrapped in the MOF HKUST-1 catalyzes carbon-nitrogen coupling to make α-ketoamides, and being magnetic means pulling it out with a magnet instead of filtering. They also ran molecular docking on the products to size up structure-affinity trends, though that part reads more exploratory than the catalysis itself.

original_title: Solid-phase synthesis and structure-degradation relationships of VHL-recruiting PROTACs for preferential histone deacetylase 6 degradation
title: Tuning the linker to make a PROTAC pick HDAC6 over its cousins
blurb: A solid-phase series of VHL-recruiting PROTACs built on a vorinostat-style HDAC inhibitor, where longer semi-rigid linkers turned out to be what drives efficient, selective HDAC6 degradation. The best compound, 15, hits a DC50 of 26 nM, with 12 degrading fastest, and both work in MM.1S myeloma cells and FLT3-ITD-positive MV4-11 leukemia cells. Getting HDAC6 without dragging down its class IIb relatives is the actual hard part.

original_title: Stabilization and Transformation of MXenes into Flexible and Thermal Oxidation-Resistant Non-van der Waals solids via Vapor-Phase Chemical Intercalation
title: Keeping MXenes from turning into rocksalt when you heat them
blurb: MXenes normally degrade into rocksalt structures at high temperature, so this stabilizes the Ti, Nb, and V transition metals with zinc vapor first, then intercalates aluminum, gallium, or indium vapor to bond the layers together. The payoff is a non-van-der-Waals solid that's flexible and resists thermal oxidation while holding onto MXene-like properties at temperatures that would normally wreck them.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Sea Cucumber-Inspired Double-Network Biopolymer Hydrogels for Programmable Soft Machines.
title: Sea cucumbers as the blueprint for a shape-shifting hydrogel
blurb: A double-network biopolymer hydrogel borrowing the sea cucumber's trick of switching between stiff and soft states, built toward soft machines that can be programmed to change shape or stiffness on demand.

original_title: Visible-Light-Induced Three-Component CH2 Insertion and Trifluoroethylation of Quinoxalin-2(1 H )-ones
title: Acetone doubles as the CH2 source in a new trifluoroethylation
blurb: A three-component, metal-free reaction that installs a trifluoroethyl group at C3 of quinoxalin-2(1H)-ones, using TFSP as the CF3 source and plain acetone as the CH2 unit. Mild conditions, broad substrate scope, and good yields across the board, for once.

original_title: PeTFlow: Flow-Matching Based All-Atom Peptide Design through Side-Chain State Tokenization
title: A peptide designer that tokenizes side chains like words
blurb: PeTFlow builds peptides to fit a target pocket by representing each residue's side-chain state as a discrete token, so sequence, backbone geometry, and side-chain packing get optimized together instead of in separate stages. Computational design only so far, no word on how the output peptides actually perform at the bench.

original_title: Solvent-Directed Self-Assembly of Chiral Metal–Organic Cages and Coordination Polymers from Identical Components and Their Circularly Polarized Luminescence
title: Same building blocks, two different chiral structures, just change the solvent
blurb: Swap the DMF/MeOH ratio and identical Zn(II) subcomponents assemble into either a discrete chiral cage or a chain polymer, both blue-emitting. The cages give the better solid-state quantum yields, and in PMMA film they show circularly polarized luminescence around |glum| ~4x10^-4, decent but not spectacular.

original_title: Tuning Glass Formation in Hybrid Crystals with Alkali Metal Crown Ether Cations for Nonlinear Optical Glass-Ceramic
title: Picking the right crown-ether guest to keep a hybrid glass from decomposing first
blurb: Stuff alkali or ammonium ions into 18-crown-6 cavities alongside a Cu2(SCN)3 anion and you get a family of polar hybrid crystals meant to melt into glass rather than cook apart. Potassium gives the closest size match in the cavity and the highest decomposition temperature of the set, which is the whole point if you want a usable nonlinear-optical glass-ceramic.

original_title: Encoding Cell‐Surface Receptor Function Through Glycosylation: Lessons From CD44
title: What kind of receptor CD44 is depends on its sugars
blurb: A review making the case that glycosylation on CD44 doesn't just fine-tune receptor activity but switches it between distinct functional states, reshaping ligand recognition and how it clusters on the cell surface. Worth it if you're still thinking of receptor identity as fixed by gene sequence alone.

original_title: Methoxy-Functionalized Coumarin-Sensitized Tris(coumarinate) Sm(III) and Dy(III) Complexes: Tunable Visible and Near-Infrared Luminescence
title: Coumarin antennas tune lanthanide glow from visible to near-IR
blurb: Pairing a methoxy-coumarin ligand with bipyridine around Sm3+ and Dy3+ gives tris(coumarinate) complexes with tunable visible and NIR emission, the Dy complex crystallizing as a solvent-free, eight-coordinate mononuclear structure. The usual lanthanide-luminophore playbook, but another ligand pushing quantum yield in the right direction still counts for something.

original_title: Advancing chemical reaction prediction in data-scarce drug discovery with active and geometric deep learning
title: An active-learning loop that tells the lab which reactions to actually run
blurb: Reaction prediction is only as good as the training data, so this closed-loop workflow uses a tree-based ensemble to pick the most informative reactions to test next, then feeds the results into a geometric deep learning model aimed at nailing regioselectivity. Built specifically for the data-scarce drug discovery case, where there's never enough logged reaction data to train on blindly.
